title: Thundering-herd prevention and KV-slot reclaim plan for continuous batcher
creator: Leah Park
description: On 2025-11-01 at ~09:30 UTC we observed repeated episodes where the continuous batcher stopped forming usable batches for 15–90s windows under a sudden traffic burst from a single high-QPS route. Symptoms included a rapid rise in request queue depth, GPU workers idling despite high queue length, and a spike in 99.9th-percentile response latency from ~120ms to ~2.4s for affected routes. The incident was not a full outage but caused significant tail-latency regressions for a subset of customers using short-prefix chat prompts. This ticket captures the post-incident analysis, short-term mitigations, and longer-term fixes focused on KV-slot reclamation, fairness, and adaptive coalescing to prevent thundering-herd-style stalls.
postmortem_summary: A combination of (1) KV-cache slot leaking on aborted requests, (2) aggressive coalescing window tuning tuned for latency (very small windows), and (3) scheduler queue ordering interaction caused a 'thundering herd' where many cold-prefix requests arrived simultaneously and blocked batch formation. Immediate mitigations patched slot reclamation and introduced a conservative fallback coalescing mode. Long-term actions include an adaptive coalescing algorithm, fairness-aware admission, improved observability, and a hard reclamation path for KV slots tied to timeouts.
root_cause: KV cache slots were not reclaimed in ~0.3% of cold-start request abort paths due to an early-return path missing release call (race with async writeback)
Batcher coalescing windows configured aggressively (2ms target) caused small batches that could not satisfy kernel-min-batch constraints under bursty single-route traffic
Scheduler ordering allowed priority inversion: long-waiting requests could be overtaken by newer but larger requests because of coalescer-driven queue reshuffle
Insufficient observability: no per-route batch-formation latency histogram and no end-to-end metric linking KV-slot occupancy to batcher throughput
detection: Detected by SLO alert on route 'chat-short-prefix' 99.9p latency and by increased batcher-queue-length alerts. Pager escalated at 09:45 UTC after automated rollout mitigation did not activate. Incident channel #inc-batching-thundering-herd was created; on-call reproduced with local load generator.
impact: Tail latency P99.9 regressions on 6 customer routes for 30–90 minutes; increased token/unit cost for some customers due to reattempts. No data loss. Some Dedicated customers saw degraded UX; one customer engaged support and requested a timeline for fixes.
mitigations_taken: Hotfix: ensure KV-slot release on all request abort paths (PR #rwd/infra/kv-reclaim-21345)
Temporarily widen coalescing window to 6ms for affected routes and enable conservative-mode for routes with >80% cold-prefix rate
Add temporary admission throttling per-route when batcher backlog exceeds 2x baseline to prevent head-of-line blocking
Rollback recent micro-tuning change to coalescer parameters that reduced batch-formation grace by 50%
action_items: (A1) Implement adaptive coalescing: coalescing window scales with observed arrival variance and kernel-min-batch. Owner: Rajat Mehra. Est: 5pt. Due: 2025-12-05.
(A2) Add hard KV-slot reclamation timeout: if slot unused for X ms after abort, forcibly free and increment reclaim metrics. Owner: Priya Desai. Est: 3pt. Due: 2025-11-20.

(A3) Introduce per-route 'batch-formation-latency' & 'kv-slot-occupancy' histograms, plus a composite SLO that ties slot occupancy > 70% to alerting. Owner: Observability team (Dan Kim). Est: 3pt. Due: 2025-11-28.
(A4) Fairness-aware admission: enforce max inflight per logical-key (customer/route) and degrade large bursts gracefully. Owner: Serving Runtime (Marina Kovács). Est: 8pt. Due: 2026-01-10.
(A5) End-to-end chaos test for bursty cold-prefix traffic to validate coalescing, KV reclaim, and scheduler interaction. Owner: SRE (Alex Nguyen). Est: 5pt. Due: 2025-12-12.

(A6) Post-deploy runbook update: include throttling thresholds, emergency widen-window knob, and step-by-step rollback for recent coalescer tuning. Owner: Runbooks (Leah Park). Est: 2pt. Due: 2025-11-18.
